chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, regarding the supplication for the child.

He said: Pour upon yourself a bucket from the water of Zamzam, then enter the House. So when you stand at the door of the House, take the ring of the door, then say: 'O Allah, the House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and You have said: 'And whoever enters it shall be secure', therefore secure me from Your punishment, and rescue me from Your wrath.'

Then enter the House, so perform two rak'at of prayer upon the red marble slab. Then stand before the pillar which is opposite the Stone, and press your chest against it, then say: 'O One, O the Alone, O the Glorious, O the Near, O the Remote, O the Mighty, O the Wise, Do not leave me alone, and You are the Best of inheritors, Endow to me from Yourself a goodly offspring. You are the Hearer of the supplication.'
Then circle by the pillar, and press your back and belly against it, and supplicate with this supplication. So if Allah wills something, it will happen.
ai.seo_question: What is the ritual supplication for having children according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This supplication, transmitted via Safwan ibn Yahya in Al-Kafi, outlines a specific ritual for seeking offspring by combining physical acts of devotion—such as pressing against the pillar opposite the Black Stone—with recitation of divine attributes like 'Al-Wahid' and 'Al-Ahad'. It reflects the Shia emphasis on linking Quranic promises of divine protection and responsiveness to tangible acts of worship within the sanctity of the Kaaba.
